question: How long do we have to close an NCR?
reply: Close each NCR within 30 calendar days of detection, or record the reason for the extension in the NCR [QMS-003 v1.0 §7.1.2]. Quality Assurance closes the NCR [QMS-003 v1.0 §7.1.2]. Closure requires that the disposition is complete, the final status is set and any CAPA number is linked [QMS-003 v1.0 §6.7.2].

question: What is the analytical flow rate and the total run time of the LC method?
reply:
Analytical flow is 5 µL/min (two nano pumps combined), through the trap column onto the analytical column [TM-104 v1.0 §7.2]. Total run time is 8 min, starting at injection (time zero). This does not include the time the autosampler needs to draw the sample [TM-104 v1.0 §7.2].

If the method file differs from the §7.2 table, do not acquire and follow TM-104 §8.3 [TM-104 v1.0 §7.2].

question: What signal-to-noise ratio must the heavy (SIS) peak of a sample well reach, and what happens if it does not?
reply:
The heavy (SIS) peak of a sample well must have S/N > 5 [TM-105 v2.0 §8.2]. S/N is calculated as Total Area ÷ Total Background [TM-105 v2.0 §7.3.1].

If it fails, the Associate Scientist marks that protein result of the sample "invalid – SIS failure" [TM-105 v2.0 §7.3.4]. The Associate Scientist then follows TM-105 §8.3 for each such result as a sample-level nonconformity [TM-105 v2.0 §7.3.5].

The excerpts do not include TM-105 §8.3, so the steps of that nonconformity handling are not covered by the effective SOPs.

question: A batch analysis started under TM-105 v1.0 was not finished when v2.0 became effective. Can I finish it under v1.0?
reply:
No. A batch whose analysis under TM-105 v1.0 is not complete on the effective date of TM-105 v2.0 is analysed again from TM-105 §7.1.1 under v2.0, because v1.0 is then Superseded [TM-105 v2.0 §2.4.1]. Each batch is analysed under one TM-105 version from start to end [TM-105 v2.0 §2.4].

Conditions for the re-analysis:
- Start again from the raw data files, in a new Skyline document created from TM-105-T01 [TM-105 v2.0 §2.4.2].
- Do not open the stored v1.0 Skyline document in the new Skyline version or save it again [TM-105 v2.0 §2.4.2].
- Training on v1.0 does not qualify an Associate Scientist or Technical Reviewer for v2.0. Training on v2.0 is recorded before first use [TM-105 v2.0 §2.4.3].

question: Where do I record a manual peak integration in Skyline?
reply:
Record the reason for each manual integration in the Skyline audit log. The reason you enter must be the permitted condition from the manual integration table of TM-105 §7.2, and it is mandatory. [TM-105 v2.0 §7.2 step 7.2.6]

Manual integration is allowed only for the conditions in that table: a peak where the light and heavy apexes differ by more than the co-elution limit, or a peak Skyline flags as truncated. [TM-105 v2.0 §7.2 step 7.2.8]

If no permitted condition applies, do not adjust the peak. [TM-105 v2.0 §7.2 step 7.2.7]
